root_idea.summary: The root centers on something pouring forth after fullness, especially a full bucket and the water poured from it.
root_idea.development: From the concrete image of a full bucket and pouring water, the lexicon develops meanings of abundant giving, shares distributed in turn, reciprocal competition, and things made freely available. The connection of the record-word سِجِلّ and the punishment-word سِجِّيل to this development is discussed but not uniform.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested noun, normalized to the classical citation form سِجِّيلٌ.
Distinct Quran-attested noun, normalized to the classical citation form سِجِلٌّ.

senses.definition: Stones or lumps of baked, hard clay.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in Quranic descriptions of punishment. Explanations include stones of clay baked by the fire and the sense “many and hard.”

senses.definition: What has been written or decreed for a people as the punishment destined for them.
senses.usage_conditions: An alternative Quranic interpretation of مِنْ سِجِّيلٍ derives the expression from سِجِلٍّ, “what has been written or decreed.”

senses.definition: A written document, record, or scroll.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quran 21:104, the expression is interpreted as folding a scroll for writing or a written record, including the record of a person's deeds.
Reported as an interpretation of the word in the Quranic passage 21:104 rather than of the written object itself.

senses.definition: An angel who folds written records of human deeds.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quranic interpretation associated with 21:104; it identifies the referent as the angel responsible for folding such records.
Reported for the interpretation of 21:104 in an alternative reading without the article, with an explanation involving an Abyssinian-language word.
Reported as another reading in interpretations of 21:104, not as the canonical QAC form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour water out continuously; by extension, to recite the Qur'an continuously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The continuous-recitation use is a derived Quranic expression cited in the lexical discussion, though no corresponding QAC verb form is present in this packet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To write or enter a record, especially a judicial record; to decide, decree, or establish something judicially and record it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Commonly said of a judge or decision recorded in a سِجِلّ; it may also mean securing property by judicial decision.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone notorious for something or stigmatize him by it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use of the transitive Form II verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To throw something down from above.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate Form II lexical use, with the verbal noun سَجْلٌ also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become affected by carnal appetite.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported Form II use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To vie, compete, contend for superiority, emulate, or rival one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The original image is two people drawing equal bucketfuls of water; the use extends to competition in running, watering, or other matters. The saying الحَرْبُ سِجَالٌ describes victory alternating between opponents.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pour or flow forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said especially of water that becomes poured out or flows forth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A full or great bucket, a bucket containing water, or the quantity that fills a bucket.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An empty bucket is not called سَجْلٌ in the cited usage; the noun is treated as masculine and its plural is سِجَالٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A share or portion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom الحَرْبُ سِجَالٌ presents war as an alternating distribution of portions or victories; سَجْلٌ may also mean someone's allotted share of something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A gift or benefaction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metaphorical extension from a bucketful or abundant outpouring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bountiful or generous man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description based on abundant giving.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A great udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or descriptive nominal use; the reported plural forms include سِجَالٌ and سُجُولٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give a bucketful or two, or to give much; to abound in goodness, beneficence, and gifts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The meanings of abundant giving and abounding in beneficence are treated as one Form IV branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a watering-trough or tank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also reported with the Form I verb سَجَلَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To send forth, set loose, or free.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a beast released with its mother and, in a traditional expression, of cattle being let loose.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave people or leave them alone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct Form IV use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make an affair free or allowable to people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative Form IV use concerning permission or unrestricted availability.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make speech or language unrestricted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use concerning the removal of restriction from speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To write a document or piece of writing for someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV writing use, with the verbal noun إِسْجَالٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ewe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical noun reported in this form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A call used when a ewe is to be milked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic reduplicated expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-goat abundant in milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A textual correction in the cited lexicographical tradition gives this as the primary reading; a variant would yield a spring or eye abundant in water or tears.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Large or big, especially a large bucket.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective may also be used substantively for a large bucket.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Long, pendent, or wide in reference to an udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: One reported specification applies the wide, flaccid, pendulous description to the udder of a sheep or goat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Flaccid and wide in the scrotum, of a testicle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical descriptive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hard and strong.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported adjectival use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A share or portion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as an analysis of the form derived from سَجْلٌ meaning a full bucket or a share; the analysis is attributed to one authority with reservation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Flaccidity and wideness in the scrotum, of a testicle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun corresponding to the cited descriptive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Permanent or lasting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical Arabic use reported separately from the Quranic noun's physical and interpretive meanings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A mirror, including a Chinese mirror.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is reported as Arabicized, with زَجَنْجَلٌ also occurring as a variant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece of silver shaped like or called a mirror.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or transferred use based on the mirror term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Gold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Saffron.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately reported lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Long or large in the udder, of a she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use applied specifically to a she-camel in the cited evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Large in the posterior parts, of a woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival use explicitly applied to a woman in the cited evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unrestricted, allowable, or open to everyone; not denied to anyone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In a Quran-quoted explanation of 55:60, the recompense is described as applying without restriction to the righteous and the unrighteous alike. It can also describe a time or fortune when no one feared anyone.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Making someone notorious or stigmatizing him.
Giving one or two bucketfuls or giving much.
Releasing a beast with its mother.
Abounding in goodness, beneficence, and gifts.
Full or great bucket and bucketful.
Share, portion, and alternating war fortunes.
Written object and alternative Quranic interpretations.
Call to a ewe to be milked.
Flaccidity and wideness of a testicle.
Silver pieces likened to a mirror.

cautions: سِجِّيلٌ has competing lexical explanations in the Classical sources, including baked clay, hard or many stones, and what has been written or decreed; these are kept as distinct Quranic senses where materially different.

The writer, angel, man, and dial interpretations attached to سِجِلٌّ concern alternative readings or exegeses of Quran 21:104 and should not be treated as equally certain identifications of the canonical QAC form.
